summary: Midday metering attenuation after cache TTL invalidation causing under-billed invoice line and provisional credit request
description: Issue summary: BrightRoutes reported a missing invoice line for 2026-01-20 12:00-15:00 UTC in their finalized invoice. They observed a ~45% drop in recorded token usage for the midday window compared to expected traffic. Impact: Under-billing observed on a finalized invoice; customer requests provisional credit while we investigate root cause. Timeline: 2026-01-20 12:10 UTC customer opened chat to billing; 2026-01-20 13:00 support ticket opened; 2026-01-20 18:00 customer uploaded sample request IDs. Environment: prod (eu-west), BrightRoutes on Dedicated pool BR-DED-004. Relevant notes: Traffic pattern unchanged on customer side; requests show successful 200 responses in application logs. Suspected area: metering-service aggregation after kv-cache TTL invalidation at 12:00 UTC caused intermittent microbatch drops and loss of token counts in hourly accumulator. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run a controlled microbatch stream using BrightRoutes API key in prod eu-west during a scheduled kv-cache TTL boundary. 2) Verify ingested events reach metering-service and are forwarded to billing-processor. 3) Observe hourly accumulator delta vs raw token log. Attachments/links: customer supplied sample request IDs and timestamps (see comments), billing dashboard snapshot, and span logs from ingest-proxy.

2026-01-20 14:20 - Diego Fernandez: Acknowledged. Requested sample request IDs and latest finalized invoice PDF. Asked SRE to pull metering-service logs for 12:00-15:00 UTC.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: TTL boundary on kv-cache triggered a short window where aggregated microbatches were not committed to the hourly accumulator due to a race in the metering-service 'flush_on_evict' path.

Hypothesis B: Ingest-proxy backpressure resulted in silent drop of non-critical telemetry events that metering-service uses to correlate request fragments; application responses were still proxied, so customer app saw no errors.

Logs (summary): metering-service logs show 'flush_on_evict: commit-failed: context deadline exceeded' at 12:00:05Z repeated ~8 times. Billing-processor accepted the downstream postbacks for surrounding minutes but missing batch for 12:00-12:05 UTC. Ingest-proxy trace shows elevated latency but no 5xx.

Reproduction attempts: Replayed batch with identical size in staging with TTL boundary present and observed a ~30-50% reduction in hourly accumulator delta because the local accumulator refused late commits during eviction. Root cause narrowed to a race condition introduced by kv-cache eviction handler in version v1.8.2 of metering-service.

Scope: So far only confirmed for dedicated pools where kv-cache TTL is set to 3600s and eviction coincides with microbatch flushing. Likely affects other dedicated customers on eu-west with similar TTL schedules.
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/4123 contains a proposed fix to make flush_on_evict idempotent and resilient to commit timeouts.
resolution_notes: Workaround (applied): Issued provisional credit of 325.50 USD to BrightRoutes invoice on 2026-01-22 and flagged account with 'billing-review' until postmortem complete.

Fix (planned): Patch metering-service v1.8.3 to make 'flush_on_evict' retriable and to persist microbatch to durable queue before eviction. PR #4123 opened; target canary deploy in eu-west 2026-01-25.

Follow-ups: 1) Run targeted audit for other dedicated customers with kv-cache TTL alignment during the last 30 days. 2) Add telemetry alert for 'microbatch-commit failures' to trigger automated replay to billing-processor. 3) Confluence postmortem to be published after root cause verification.
Customer communication: Notified BrightRoutes of provisional credit and timeline for fix. Will confirm final adjustment after audit.
